newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil's Troll C platform may be run by electricity.
newsitem.headline: Statoil's Troll C platform may be run by electricity.

text.p: A proposal from Norwegian operator Norsk Hydro to prepare the new Troll C oil platform to run on electricity has won government support, Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil ) said on Thursday.

Intended to replace power generated offshore by burning gas, these plans must be seen in relation to an upgrading of Statoil's Troll A gas platform after the year 2000, state-owned Statoil's Status Weekly newsletter said.
Using land-based power supplies would reduce emissions of carbon dioxide from the North Sea installation, it said.

"Troll A already runs on about three megawatts of hydropower received by cable from Kollsnes north of Bergen. As pressure in the reservoir declines, however, its electricity needs will rise to 160 megawatts," Status Weekly said.

Due to come on stream in autumn 1999, Troll C requires some 60 megawatts. The combined requirements of the two platforms correspond to almost two-thirds of output from the planned gas-fired power station at Kollsnes, it said.
"Should the latter facility be shelved, a new transmission line may have to be built to Kollsnes," Oeyvind Kirkhus of Statoil's Troll organisation said.

Power demand by Troll's land-based installations and offshore platforms will exceed today's electricity transmission capacity. But the local population has already protested strongly against existing power lines to Kollsnes, Status Weekly said.
